COVID-19 and pursuant to AB 361. All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which
will be live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged
to submit email correspondence to mlinden@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may also speak
during the meeting through the Zoom application. You must first sign up to speak before the item
you would like to speak on has been called and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to
speak and to download the Zoom application.

  B.  Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Fourth Quarter Financial Report
  Recommended Action: Review Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Fourth Quarter financial
  information.

  Assistant City Manager Toney thanked the Finance team for their ongoing efforts
  to keep the City’s financial status in order and for their assistance in compiling the
  financial reports. He presented the report and highlighted accounts with significant
  numbers related to the budget.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, City Manager McClary stated Public Safety
  Director Dueñas and Lieutenant Chad Watters found savings for the City related to
  the Beach Team.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated the budget ended in a great position with an
  extremely healthy reserve balance as of the end of Fiscal Year 2021-2022.

  Councilmember Uhring asked if the number of short-term rentals had increased.
  Assistant City Manager Toney stated he would look into that but expected there
  was some increase as the pandemic restrictions eased.

  Councilmember Pierson stated the number of short-term rentals had not increased
  as much as he had expected. He stated the transient occupancy tax (TOT) increase
  was working out well. He stated the upcoming increase in sales tax would be
  beneficial. He noted the significant decrease in salaries.

  Councilmember Uhring and Councilmember Pierson commended staff for an
  excellent report.

  Councilmember Pierson stated the Finance team had always been solid. He stated
  it made a big difference.

  Councilmember Uhring commended Finance Manager Neermann and her team.

  C.  Fiscal Year 2022-2023 First Quarter Financial Report
  Recommended Action: Review Fiscal Year 2022-2023 First Quarter financial
  information.

  Assistant City Manager Toney presented the report. He stated there were few
  modifications so far, as those usually began in the second quarter. He stated he

  expected the major revenues of property tax, sales tax, and TOT to continue strong.
  He stated the Transactions and Use Tax (TUT) increase would go into effect on
  April 1, 2023. He stated the conservative budgeting would continue into the
  upcoming fiscal year.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed the impact of outdoor dining on sales tax
  revenues. He stated the possible change in that when the pandemic ends should be
  kept in mind when preparing future budgets.

  Doug Stewart, Councilmember-elect, discussed his corporate experience with an
  emphasis on cash management. He discussed the $83 million in uninvested funds.
  He suggested putting cash management tools back in place and reinvesting those
  funds. He stated projected reserves should be used for one-time expenditures or to
  pay down City debt.

  Councilmember Uhring suggested Mr. Stewart talk with City Treasurer Quinto. He
  requested an update on the status of the new permitting software. Assistant City
  Manager Toney stated RFP responses were currently being reviewed.

  Councilmember Pierson agreed that Mr. Stewart should talk with City Treasurer
  Quinto about the City’s positions and options for investment. He agreed with Mr.
  Stewart that this might be a good time for certain one-time expenditures. He stated
  he was pleased revenue from the new sales tax increase would come to the City and
  not the County.

  City Manager McClary discussed recent news that the State was projecting a
  potential $25 billion deficit in the coming year. He stated staff would watch that
  closely for potential impacts on the City. He stated City-specific revenues were
  secure.

  Assistant City Manager Toney presented the report. He thanked the Finance team

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, Assistant City Manager Toney confirmed the
  hazard tree grant was received and would be offset by the expenditure. Mayor
  Silverstein stated it would be helpful to see income from permits with the related

  C.  Investment Report
  Recommended Action: Review Investment Policy compliance and provide
  feedback to staff.

  City Treasurer Quinto presented the report. She stated a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) for the City’s financial institutions had not been conducted as required by
  the Investment Policy. She stated an RFP for banking services and more timely
  reporting would be implemented in the near future.

  In response to Councilmember Stewart, City Treasurer Quinto stated 110 percent
  was maintained in a separate custodial account. Councilmember Stewart stated the
  auditors did not test the City’s investment policy. He stated $91 million of
  investible funds could be earning $4.5 million. He stated the City was earning about
  one-half of the benchmark. He questioned why the benchmark was not reported.
  He suggested $80 million could be converted to six-month investments. He
  suggested the City be more proactive.

  City Treasurer Quinto confirmed the City was not as active as it could be to increase
  the yield. She stated $12 million in the operating checking account was reasonable.
  She stated the entire $90 million Reserve was not investible. She stated the two-
  year treasury note did not include the current benchmark rate. She stated a different
  level of action was appropriate for current interest rates.

  Councilmember Stewart agreed that cash management and investments had
  become far more important over the past year. In response to Councilmember

  in 2012. In response to Mayor Silverstein, City Treasurer Quinto stated the
  investments listed as Wells Fargo could be with other banks but were sold to the

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, William Gomberg, Wells Fargo Advisors,

  certificates of deposit (CDs) from any individual bank was limited to $250,000 for

  of money market accounts. He stated Wells Fargo could utilize the money market

Subject:  Proposed Schedule of Fees Fiscal Year 2023-24

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide a recommendation to the City Council concerning
adoption of the Fiscal Year 2023-24 Schedule of Fees.

FISCAL IMPACT: The Schedule of Fees establishes the amount the City can charge for
fees for service. The City’s annual budget typically includes approximately $5.0 million in
revenue from Service Charges and approximately $3.5 million in revenue from Licenses
and Permits.

DISCUSSION: For Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-24, departmental staff reviewed all fees to
ensure that charges for specific services appropriately cover the cost of providing such
service. If the FY 2023-24 fee schedule is approved, the revised fees will generate funds
to adequately reflect the costs of the services provided.

State law mandates that agencies such as the City of Malibu charge customers only the
fees necessary to recover costs for the services provided and prohibits charging fees
above and beyond the services rendered. If the FY 2023-24 fee schedule is approved, the
revised fees will not generate funds that exceed this standard.

In FY 2015-16, the City completed a comprehensive fee study that analyzed all fees and
charges for services. The rates established in the fee study are used as a base amount
that is increased with a cost-of-living adjustment.

The cost-of-living adjustment is derived from the Consumer Price Index (CPI) using an
annual percentage from February. The percentage change of CPI was 5.1% in February
2023, and this adjustment has been included in the Schedule of Fees for FY 2023-24.
